newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian c.bank says buys hard currency from banks.
newsitem.headline: Croatian c.bank says buys hard currency from banks.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Tuesday it had intervened on the foreign exchange market by buying hard currency from the banking sector.
The bank bought 22 million German marks at an average rate of 3.5643 kuna and $2.0 million at an average 6.0227 kuna per dollar, it said in a news release.
The central bank will issue kuna to commercial banks in two days and boost money supply for some 90 million kuna.

Due to stronger tourism inflows during the summer, it usually buys more foreign currency from banks and exchange offices in part also to prevent a stronger nominal appreciation of the kuna exchange rate.
The kuna was quoted at 6.0185 to the dollar and 3.5716 to the mark before today's intervention. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
